name: First-order signature (language)
description: A specification of constant symbols, function symbols, and relation symbols together with their arities, fixing the non-logical vocabulary of a first-order language.

name: L-structure
description: A nonempty set M together with interpretations of each constant, function, and relation symbol of a signature L as actual elements, functions, and relations on M.

name: L-term
description: A syntactic expression built from variables and constant symbols by repeated application of function symbols of the signature L.

name: L-formula
description: A well-formed syntactic expression built from atomic formulas (equalities and relation symbols applied to terms) using Boolean connectives and quantifiers over variables.

name: Tarski satisfaction relation
description: The recursively defined relation specifying when an L-structure M with a variable assignment makes an L-formula true, giving the semantics of first-order logic.

name: L-embedding
description: An injective map between L-structures preserving the interpretation of all constants, functions, and relations (and their negations on atomic formulas).

name: Substructure / extension
description: An L-structure M whose domain is a subset of N closed under N's functions and constants, with all symbols interpreted as restrictions of N's interpretations.

name: L-theory
description: A set of L-sentences (closed formulas), the models of which are the L-structures satisfying every sentence in the set.

name: Logical consequence (semantic entailment)
description: The relation holding when every model of a theory T also satisfies the sentence φ.

name: Axiomatizable theory
description: A theory closed under logical consequence that is the set of consequences of some (often finite or recursive) set of axioms.

name: Definable function and definable closure
description: A function whose graph is a definable set, and the definable closure dcl(A) consisting of all elements that are the unique realization of some formula over A.

name: Henkin construction
description: Expand T to a maximal consistent theory with witnessing constants for every existential sentence, then build a model out of equivalence classes of closed terms.

name: Tarski–Vaught test
description: A substructure M of N is an elementary substructure iff for every formula φ(x,b) with parameters in M that has a solution in N, it already has a solution in M.

name: Tarski's elementary chain theorem
description: The union of an elementary chain of L-structures is an elementary extension of each member of the chain.

name: Diagram lemma
description: Models of the atomic (elementary) diagram of M correspond exactly to L-structures admitting an embedding (elementary embedding) of M.

name: Elementary diagram
description: The set of all L_M-sentences true in M after adjoining a new constant for each element of M; its models are the elementary extensions of M.

name: Upward Löwenheim–Skolem theorem
description: Any infinite structure has elementary extensions of every cardinality κ ≥ max(|M|,|L|).

name: Löwenheim–Skolem–Tarski theorem
description: A first-order theory with an infinite model has a model of every cardinality κ ≥ |L|+ℵ₀.

name: Dense linear order without endpoints (DLO)
description: The complete ℵ₀-categorical theory of a dense linear order having no least and no greatest element.

name: Robinson's test for model completeness
type_signature: (∀ M,N ⊨ T, M⊆N: ∃-formulas preserved up) ⟹ T model complete
description: A theory is model complete iff every embedding between its models preserves existential formulas, equivalently every formula is equivalent to an existential one.

name: Quantifier elimination test
description: A theory admits quantifier elimination iff for any two models with a common substructure A, a primitive existential formula realized in one over A is realized in the other (a back-and-forth/substructure-completeness criterion).

name: Completeness and decidability of ACF_p
description: For each fixed characteristic, the theory of algebraically closed fields is complete and decidable, a consequence of its quantifier elimination.

name: Lefschetz principle
description: A first-order sentence holds in the complex field iff it holds in every algebraically closed field of characteristic 0 (and in characteristic p for all large p), by completeness of ACF.

name: Ax's theorem (injective endomorphisms are surjective)
type_signature: f: V→V injective polynomial map ⟹ surjective
description: Every injective polynomial map of an algebraic variety over an algebraically closed field to itself is surjective, proved by transfer from finite fields.

name: Completeness and decidability of RCF
description: The theory of real closed ordered fields is complete and decidable, following from Tarski's quantifier elimination for RCF.

name: Hilbert's 17th problem (model-theoretic form)
description: Every positive semidefinite rational function over a real closed field is a sum of squares of rational functions, derived via the model completeness of RCF.

name: Quantifier elimination for Presburger arithmetic
description: The first-order theory of the additive integers admits quantifier elimination in the language expanded by congruence-mod-n predicates.

name: Omitting Types Theorem
type_signature: non-isolated type p ⟹ ∃ countable M omitting p
description: A countable theory has a countable model omitting any given non-isolated (non-principal) partial type, generalizable to countably many such types.

name: Isolated (principal) type
description: A complete type generated by a single formula φ, i.e. an isolated point of the Stone space of types, realized in every model containing A.

name: Prime model
description: A model of a complete theory that elementarily embeds into every other model of the theory.

name: Atomic model
description: A model in which every tuple realizes an isolated (principal) complete type over the empty set.

name: Prime ⟺ countable atomic
description: For a complete countable theory, a model is prime iff it is countable and atomic, and such a model is unique up to isomorphism when it exists.

name: Existence and uniqueness of prime/atomic models
description: A complete countable theory has a (unique up to isomorphism) prime model iff the isolated types are dense in every Stone space Sₙ(∅).

name: Uniqueness of saturated models
type_signature: two κ-saturated models of card κ ⟹ isomorphic
description: Any two saturated models of a complete theory having the same cardinality are isomorphic, proved by a back-and-forth argument.

name: Uniqueness of homogeneous models
type_signature: same card + same realized types ⟹ isomorphic
description: Two homogeneous models of the same cardinality realizing exactly the same types are isomorphic.

name: Universal model
description: A model into which every model of the theory of cardinality at most |M| elementarily embeds.

name: Monster model
description: A very large saturated and strongly homogeneous model serving as a universal domain inside which all small models and all types under study are realized.

name: Ehrenfeucht–Mostowski type (EM-type)
type_signature: Φ: order type ↦ type of indiscernibles
description: The complete type, indexed by increasing tuples, shared by an order-indiscernible sequence, determining a functor from linear orders to models.

name: Existence of indiscernibles
type_signature: any infinite (M, I) ⟹ ∃ indiscernible J realizing EM-type
description: For any theory with infinite models and any infinite linear order, there is a model containing a sequence of order-indiscernibles, obtained via Ramsey's theorem and compactness.

name: Few types over EM models
description: A model generated as the Skolem hull of order-indiscernibles realizes only few types over itself, used to control the number of types and models.

name: Vaughtian pair
description: A pair of models M ≺ N with M ≠ N but having the same infinite solution set for some formula φ, witnessing a two-cardinal phenomenon.

name: Uncountably categorical theories have no Vaughtian pairs
description: An uncountably categorical complete theory admits no Vaughtian pairs, a key step in the proof of Morley's theorem.

name: Morley degree
description: For a definable set of finite Morley rank, the maximum number of disjoint definable subsets of the same rank, measuring multiplicity at that rank.

name: Totally transcendental theory
type_signature: every formula has ordinal Morley rank
description: A theory in which every definable set has an ordinal-valued Morley rank, equivalent to ω-stability for countable languages.

name: ω-stable ⟹ totally transcendental
description: An ω-stable theory is totally transcendental, so every definable set carries a well-defined Morley rank and degree.

name: Definability of types (and heirs)
description: In a stable (in particular ω-stable) theory, every type over a model is definable, giving canonical extensions (heirs and coheirs) to larger sets.

name: Uncountably categorical ⟹ ω-stable
description: Every uncountably categorical countable complete theory is ω-stable, a central lemma in Morley's categoricity theorem.

name: ω-stable group / group of finite Morley rank
description: A group definable in an ω-stable theory, whose definable subsets carry Morley rank and degree, modeling algebraic-group-like behavior.

name: Descending chain condition on definable subgroups
type_signature: no infinite descending chain of definable subgroups
description: In an ω-stable (finite Morley rank) group there is no infinite strictly descending chain of definable subgroups, yielding a connected component.

name: Connected component G⁰
description: The smallest definable subgroup of finite index in a group of finite Morley rank, normal in G, called the connected component.

name: Generic type of a group
description: A type of an element of a finite-Morley-rank group whose Morley rank equals that of the whole group, invariant under translation in the connected case.

name: Stabilizer of a type
description: The definable subgroup of group elements fixing the (translated) type p, central to analyzing generic data in finite-Morley-rank groups.

name: Zilber indecomposability theorem
type_signature: family of indecomposable Xᵢ ∋ 1 ⟹ ⟨Xᵢ⟩ definable connected
description: In a group of finite Morley rank, the subgroup generated by a family of definable indecomposable subsets each containing the identity is definable and connected, an analogue of indecomposable algebraic subsets generating subgroups.

name: Macintyre's theorem
description: Every infinite ω-stable field is algebraically closed.

name: ω-stable division rings are commutative
description: An infinite division ring whose theory is ω-stable is commutative, hence an algebraically closed field.

name: Algebraic closure gives a pregeometry
description: On a strongly minimal set, the model-theoretic algebraic closure operator satisfies finite character, monotonicity, idempotence, and exchange, forming a pregeometry.

name: Exchange property for acl (Steinitz exchange)
description: In a strongly minimal theory, if a is algebraic over B together with c but not over B alone, then c is algebraic over B and a, the abstract Steinitz exchange axiom.

name: Pregeometry (combinatorial geometry)
description: A set with a closure operator satisfying reflexivity, monotonicity, finite character, idempotence, and the exchange property, abstracting linear/algebraic dependence (a matroid-like structure).

name: Dimension and independence in a pregeometry
description: The common cardinality of any maximal independent (closure-free) subset of a set, well-defined by the exchange property and additive over closures.

name: Dimension determines the model
description: Two models of a strongly minimal theory are isomorphic iff their associated pregeometries have the same dimension, the mechanism behind uncountable categoricity.

name: Trivial (degenerate) geometry
description: A pregeometry in which the closure of any set is the union of the closures of its points, exhibiting no nontrivial dependence.

name: Locally modular geometry
type_signature: modularity of cl over a point
description: A pregeometry that becomes modular after localizing at a single point, equivalently dim(A∪B)+dim(A∩B)=dim(A)+dim(B) for closed sets with nonempty intersection.

name: Locally modular ⟺ no definable field
description: A non-trivial strongly minimal set is non-locally-modular iff it interprets an infinite field (an algebraically closed field), linking geometry to definable algebraic structure.

name: Zilber's trichotomy conjecture
type_signature: strongly minimal ⟹ trivial / modular group / ACF
description: The conjecture that every strongly minimal set is either trivial, the geometry of a modular group (vector-space-like), or interprets an algebraically closed field; true for Zariski geometries, false in general.

name: Locally modular ⟹ group-based geometry
description: A non-trivial locally modular strongly minimal set interprets an abelian group whose geometry is essentially that of a vector space over a division ring (group configuration / 1-basedness).

name: Model completeness of ACF
description: The theory of algebraically closed fields is model complete: every embedding between algebraically closed fields is elementary, equivalently a Nullstellensatz statement.

name: Robinson's test application to ACF/RCF
description: A model-complete theory with a model embedding into every model (e.g. the prime field) is complete, used to derive completeness of ACF_p and RCF.
